data.output:
{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script (translated from PBS)

# PBS requested (templated):
#   -N analysis
#   -q batch
#   -l walltime=<walltime>
#   -l pmem=<memory>
#   -l nodes=1:ppn=1
#   -o "<out_folder>/${PBS_JOBID}.out"
#   -j oe

flux alloc \
  -N 1 \
  -n 1 \
  --queue=batch \
  bash -lc '

# NOTE: PBS walltime=<walltime> is a placeholder, so no concrete Flux --time value can be set.
# Performance implication: the job may run with site default walltime, risking premature termination or longer queue time.

# NOTE: PBS pmem=<memory> is a placeholder and also PBS-specific (per-process memory).
# Flux has no universally portable memory directive in a batch script.
# Performance implication: without a memory request/limit, placement may not account for memory needs, increasing OOM risk.

# PBS -j oe (join stdout/stderr): approximate by redirecting stderr to stdout.
# PBS -o used a placeholder path; we approximate with Flux job id.
mkdir -p "<out_folder>"
exec >"<out_folder>/${FLUX_JOB_ID}.out" 2>&1

cd "${PBS_O_WORKDIR:-$PWD}"

PROJECT_HOME="<project_home>"

PYTHONPATH="$PROJECT_HOME/libs:$PYTHONPATH"
export PYTHONPATH

if [ -d "$PROJECT_HOME/venv" ]; then
	source "$PROJECT_HOME"/venv/bin/activate
	echo "Virtualenv at $PROJECT_HOME/venv activated."
else
	echo "WARNING: Virtualenv not found/activated! Using system python & LAMMPS..."
fi

python "$PROJECT_HOME"/tools/dump_processing.py "<cfg_file>" <aargs>
'
"
}
